claim: Allergic asthma is a common childhood illness and can be triggered by exposure to aeroallergens such as house dust mite (HDM).
source: Allergic asthma is a common childhood illness and can be triggered by exposure to aeroallergens such as house dust mite (HDM).
evidence: This is a statement of established medical knowledge about allergic asthma etiology.

claim: Hallmark features of allergic asthma include aberrant T helper 2 (Th2) type responses, airway hyperreactivity, eosinophilic inflammation, increased IgE and mucus hypersecretion.
source: Hallmark features of the disease include aberrant T helper 2 (Th2) type responses, airway hyperreactivity, eosinophilic inflammation, increased IgE and mucus hypersecretion (Finkelman et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Finkelman et al., 2010.

claim: The balance between pro-inflammatory CD4+ Th2 cells and regulatory T cells is a significant determinant in the development of allergic disease.
source: The balance between pro-inflammatory CD4+ Th2 cells and regulatory T cells, including CD4+Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Treg) and CD4+Foxp3-, interleukin-10 (IL-10)-producing Type one regulatory T cells (Tr1) cells, is a significant determinant in the development of allergic disease (Robinson, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Robinson, 2009.

claim: Allergen-specific immunotherapy may re-establish tolerance in part by expanding regulatory T cell populations.
source: Allergen-specific immunotherapy may re-establish tolerance in part by expanding these regulatory T cell populations (Akdis and Akdis, 2014; Meiler et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Akdis and Akdis, 2014 and Meiler et al., 2008.

claim: The anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin 10 (IL-10) is critical for immune tolerance to airway allergens.
source: The anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin 10 (IL-10) is critical for immune tolerance to airway allergens (Hawrylowicz, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hawrylowicz, 2005.

claim: The suppressive capabilities of Tr1 cells are primarily attributed to IL-10.
source: The suppressive capabilities of Tr1 cells are primarily attributed to IL-10 while Foxp3+ T cells exert regulatory function in several ways, including via IL-10 production, (Lloyd and Hawrylowicz, 2009; Kearley et al., 2012; Wilson et al., 1992; Kearley et al., 2005; Pellerin et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: IL-10 can limit both Th2 differentiation and survival.
source: IL-10 can limit both Th2 differentiation and survival (Coomes et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Coomes et al., 2017.

claim: Endogenous T cell-derived IL-10 limits the development of pathogenic Th2 responses during allergen sensitization.
source: endogenous T cell-derived IL-10 limits the development of pathogenic Th2 responses during allergen sensitization (Wilson et al., 2007; Tournoy et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wilson et al., 2007 and Tournoy et al., 2000.

claim: The development of Tr1-like cells is critical to the success of allergen-specific immunotherapy.
source: Indeed, the development of Tr1-like cells is critical to the success of allergen-specific immunotherapy (Akdis and Akdis, 2014; Meiler et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Akdis and Akdis, 2014 and Meiler et al., 2008.

claim: HDM-sensitized animals show an increase in total number of cells in the broncho-alveolar lavage (BAL) compared to controls.
source: This model recapitulates key features of allergic responses associated with type two inflammation, with HDM- sensitized animals showing an increase in total number of cells (Figure 1B)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: HDM-sensitized animals show an increase in total number of eosinophils in the BAL compared to controls.
source: with HDM- sensitized animals showing an increase in total number of cells (Figure 1B) and total number of eosinophils (Figure 1C) in the broncho-alveolar lavage (BAL) as compared to controls.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The lungs of HDM-sensitized animals exhibited an increase in peribronchiolar and perivascular inflammation.
source: Also, the lungs of HDM-sensitized animals exhibited an increase in peribronchiolar and perivascular inflammation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The levels of total IgE were elevated in the BAL supernatants obtained from HDM-sensitized animals.
source: The levels of total IgE were also elevated in the BAL supernatants obtained from HDM-sensitized animals (Figure 1E).
evidence: This statement is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The frequency of CD90.1+ Foxp3-CD4+ Tr1-like cells was increased in the HDM-sensitized animals in the BAL and the lungs.
source: Using this model, we found that the frequency of CD90.1+ Foxp3-CD4+ Tr1-like cells was increased in the HDM-sensitized animals in the BAL and the lungs (Figure 1F,G)
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 1F and 1G.

claim: The frequency of CD90.1+ Foxp3-CD4+ Tr1-like cells was not increased in the pulmonary lymph node or the spleen of HDM-sensitized animals.
source: but not in the pulmonary lymph node (Figure 1H) or the spleen (Figure 1I).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 1H and 1I.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3- Tr1-like cells specifically accumulated at the site of allergen challenge.
source: Thus, CD90.1+Foxp3- Tr1-like cells specifically accumulated at the site of allergen challenge.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing increased Tr1-like cells in BAL and lungs but not in lymph nodes or spleen.

claim: The majority of CD90.1+Foxp3-CD4+ T cells were parenchymal.
source: We found that the majority of CD90.1+Foxp3-CD4+ T cells were parenchymal (Figure 2A–D)
evidence: This statement is supported by intravascular labeling data shown in Figures 2A-D.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3+CD4+ T cells were primarily parenchymal.
source: as were the CD90.1+Foxp3+CD4+ T cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: This statement is supported by intravascular labeling data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: More than half of CD90.1-Foxp3+CD4+ T cells were in the lung vasculature.
source: In contrast more than half of CD90.1-Foxp3+CD4+ T cells and about half of the CD90.1-Foxp3- CD4+ T cells were in the lung vasculature (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This statement is supported by intravascular labeling data shown in Figures 2F-G.

claim: Both CD90.1+Foxp3- and CD90.1+Foxp3+ T cells are primarily within the lung parenchyma.
source: These data indicated that both CD90.1+Foxp3- and CD90.1+Foxp3+ T cells are primarily within the lung parenchyma.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the intravascular labeling data.

claim: In control animals, non-T cells (CD3-) comprised the majority of CD90.1+ cells.
source: In control animals, non-T cells (CD3-) comprised the majority of CD90.1+ whereas in HDM-sensitized animals, the majority of CD90.1+ were Foxp3-CD4+ T cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In HDM-sensitized animals, the majority of CD90.1+ cells were Foxp3-CD4+ T cells.
source: In control animals, non-T cells (CD3-) comprised the majority of CD90.1+ whereas in HDM-sensitized animals, the majority of CD90.1+ were Foxp3-CD4+ T cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The total number of CD90.1+ Foxp3- cells was predominantly increased in the lungs in comparison to other CD90.1+ subsets.
source: The total number of CD90.1+ Foxp3- cells was predominantly increased in the lungs in comparison to other CD90.1 + subsets (Figure 3C).
evidence: This statement is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The MFI of CD90.1 was increased in the CD90.1+Foxp3- subsets as compared to CD3+CD4- and CD3-CD4- subsets.
source: The MFI of CD90.1 as a correlate of IL-10 production was also increased in the CD90.1+Foxp3- subsets as compared to CD3+CD4- and CD3-CD4- subsets (Figure 3D).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The increase in the frequency of Tr1-like cells at the site of allergen sensitization could be attributed to the accumulation of CD90.1+ Foxp3- CD4+ T cells in the lungs.
source: Thus, the increase in the frequency of Tr1-like cells at the site of allergen sensitization could be attributed to the accumulation of CD90.1+ Foxp3- CD4+ T cells in the lungs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing increased CD90.1+Foxp3- cells in the lungs.

claim: CD25 was explicitly increased on Foxp3+ cells irrespective of IL-10 production.
source: CD25 was explicitly increased on Foxp3+ cells irrespective of IL-10 production, though CD90.1+Foxp3+ exhibited a lower level of expression in comparison to CD90.1-Foxp3+ cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Both KLRG1 and PD-1 are highly expressed on CD90.1+ cells irrespective of Foxp3 expression.
source: We found that both KLRG1 and PD-1 are highly expressed on CD90.1+ cells irrespective of Foxp3 expression (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 4B and 4C.

claim: All IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells irrespective of Foxp3 expression express high levels of CD44.
source: All IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells irrespective of Foxp3 expression express high levels of CD44 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: CD44-/- mice did not show a decrease in the frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3- or CD90.1+Foxp3+ cells in the HDM model.
source: Despite this association, CD44- /- mice did not show a decrease in the frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3- or CD90.1+Foxp3+ cells in the HDM model, suggesting that CD44 is dispensable for their induction (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data from CD44-/- mice shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD44 is dispensable for the induction of CD90.1+Foxp3- or CD90.1+Foxp3+ cells.
source: Despite this association, CD44- /- mice did not show a decrease in the frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3- or CD90.1+Foxp3+ cells in the HDM model, suggesting that CD44 is dispensable for their induction (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CD44-/- mouse data.

claim: LAG3 expression distinguished CD90.1+Foxp3- from CD90.1-Foxp3- T cells.
source: We found that while LAG3 expression distinguished CD90.1+Foxp3- from CD90.1-Foxp3- T cells, it did not distinguish between CD90.1+Foxp3- and either CD90.1+Foxp3+ cells or CD90.1-Foxp3+ cells (Figure 4H).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: LAG3 expression did not distinguish between CD90.1+Foxp3- and either CD90.1+Foxp3+ cells or CD90.1-Foxp3+ cells.
source: We found that while LAG3 expression distinguished CD90.1+Foxp3- from CD90.1-Foxp3- T cells, it did not distinguish between CD90.1+Foxp3- and either CD90.1+Foxp3+ cells or CD90.1-Foxp3+ cells (Figure 4H).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: CD49b expression was similar between all the different CD4+ T cell subsets.
source: CD49b expression was similar between all the different subsets (Figure 4I).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3- cells in this model are typically CD44hi, CD25lo, PD-1hi, LAG3hi, and KLRGint.
source: Together these data indicate that CD90.1+Foxp3- cells in this model are typically CD44hi, CD25lo, PD-1hi, LAG3hi, and KLRGint.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the phenotypic marker data.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3- cells share most markers previously associated with Tr1 cells.
source: Thus, these cells share most markers previously associated with Tr1 cells (i.e. they are 'Tr1-like').
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phenotypic marker analysis.

claim: The phenotypic markers do not distinguish between Tr1-like cells and other IL-10-producing cells in this model.
source: However, these markers do not distinguish between Tr1-like cells and other IL-10-producing cells in this model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the phenotypic marker analysis.

claim: The inflammatory response peaked on day 16 as measured by total cellular and eosinophilic infiltration in the BAL.
source: The inflammatory response peaked on day 16 as measured by total cellular (Figure 5B) and eosinophilic infiltration (Figure 5C) in the BAL.
evidence: This statement is supported by cell count data shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: By day 30, inflammation was largely resolved.
source: By day 30, inflammation was largely resolved.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic data showing decreased inflammation at day 30.

claim: The frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3- (Tr1-like cells) within the CD4+ T cell population was maximal at day 16 and waned by day 30.
source: The frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3- (Tr1-like cells) within the CD4+ T cell population was likewise maximal at day 16 and waned by day 30 (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claim: The frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3+ Treg was maximal at day 16.
source: The frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3+ Treg was also maximal at day 16 (Figure 5F)
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: At the peak of inflammation on day 16 the majority of CD90.1+ Foxp3- cells produced IL-10 and insignificant amounts of IFNg, IL-13, or IL-17 in the lungs.
source: At the peak of inflammation on day 16 the majority of CD90.1+ Foxp3- cells produced IL-10 and insignificant amounts of IFNg, IL-13, or IL-17 in the lungs (Figure 5G)
evidence: This statement is supported by intracellular cytokine staining data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: By day 30 IL-10 production by CD90.1 cells had waned.
source: However, by day 30 IL-10 production by CD90.1 cells had waned (Figure 5G).
evidence: This statement is supported by intracellular cytokine staining data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: CD90.1+IL-10- 'former Tr1' remained within the lung parenchyma.
source: These CD90.1+IL-10- 'former Tr1' remained within the lung parenchyma as assessed by intravenous labeling (Figure 5H).
evidence: This statement is supported by intravascular labeling data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The majority of CD90.1+IL-10- 'former Tr1' cells were CD62L negative and CD44 high hence exhibiting an effector memory phenotype.
source: Moreover, majority of these cells were CD62L negative and CD44 high hence exhibiting an effector memory phenotype (Figure 5I).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Tr1-like cells and not Foxp3+ Treg comprise the majority of IL-10+ T cells in this model.
source: Together, these data indicate that Tr1-like cells and not Foxp3+ Treg comprise the majority of IL-10+ T cells in this model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic and phenotypic data.

claim: Some CD90.1+ cells may contribute to the allergen specific memory T-cell pool.
source: Further, these data suggest that some CD90.1+cells may contribute to the allergen specific memory T-cell pool.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that CD90.1+ cells persist with a memory phenotype.

claim: Only cells which were activated continued to produce IL-10 after 5 days in cell culture.
source: Only cells which were activated continued to produce IL-10 after 5 days in cell culture (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by in vitro culture data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: The viability of cultured cells was severely affected in the absence of TCR stimulation over time.
source: Moreover, the viability of cultured cells was severely affected in the absence of TCR stimulation over time (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by viability data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Irf1 and Batf are upregulated only in cells actively producing IL-10.
source: We found that Irf1 and Batf are upregulated only in cells actively producing IL-10 (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This statement is supported by qPCR data shown in Figures 6C and 6D.

claim: Irf1 and Batf characterize active IL-10 production by Tr1-like cells in this model.
source: These transcription factors therefore characterize active IL-10 production by Tr1-like cells in this model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transcription factor expression data.

claim: Animals that received primary sensitization with HDM exhibited heightened airway inflammation upon rechallenge.
source: Using this protocol, we found that animals that received primary sensitization with HDM exhibited heightened airway inflammation (Figure 7B)
evidence: This statement is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Animals that received primary sensitization with HDM exhibited increased eosinophils upon rechallenge.
source: increased eosinophils (Figure 7C)
evidence: This statement is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Animals that received primary sensitization with HDM exhibited heightened IgE upon rechallenge.
source: and heightened IgE upon rechallenge (Figure 7D).
evidence: This statement is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3- cells were increased in HDM-sensitized animals upon memory rechallenge.
source: CD90.1+Foxp3- cells were increased in HDM-sensitized animals (Figure 7E)
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3+ as well as CD90.1-Foxp3+ cells were unchanged upon memory rechallenge.
source: while the frequency of CD90.1+Foxp3+ as well as CD90.1-Foxp3+ cells were unchanged.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing no change in these populations.

claim: The frequency of Foxp3-CD4+ T cells within all IL-10-producing cells was elevated in HDM-sensitized animals in comparison to control upon memory rechallenge.
source: Consequently, the frequency of Foxp3-CD4+ T cells within all IL-10-producing cells was also elevated in HDM-sensitized animals in comparison to control, although non-T cells remained the main producers of IL-10 in both groups (Figure 7F).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Non-T cells remained the main producers of IL-10 in both control and HDM-sensitized groups upon memory rechallenge.
source: although non-T cells remained the main producers of IL-10 in both groups (Figure 7F).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Most tetramer+ cells were either CD90.1+Foxp3- or CD90.1-Foxp3-.
source: Most tetramer + cells were either CD90.1+Foxp3- or CD90.1-Foxp3- while all Foxp3+ cells irrespective of CD90.1 expression were negative for tetramer staining (Figure 7G, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by tetramer staining data shown in Figure 7G and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: All Foxp3+ cells irrespective of CD90.1 expression were negative for tetramer staining.
source: Most tetramer + cells were either CD90.1+Foxp3- or CD90.1-Foxp3- while all Foxp3+ cells irrespective of CD90.1 expression were negative for tetramer staining (Figure 7G, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by tetramer staining data shown in Figure 7G and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The population of tetramer-positive Tr1-like cells increased upon antigenic challenge.
source: The population of tetramer-positive Tr1-like cells increased upon antigenic challenge while tetramer-staining Foxp3+ Treg populations did not.
evidence: This is inferred from the tetramer staining data.

claim: Within CD90.1+Foxp3-CD4+ T cells, a greater frequency of cells were tetramer+.
source: Within CD90.1+Foxp3-CD4+ T cells, a greater frequency of cells were tetramer+ (Figure 7H).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: The majority of CD90.1+Foxp3- cells produced IL-10 upon ex vivo stimulation.
source: We found that the majority of CD90.1+Foxp3- cells produced IL-10 and fewer cells produced other cytokines such as IL-4, IL-13, IFNg and IL-17 (Figure 7I, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by intracellular cytokine staining data shown in Figure 7I and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Tr1-like cells expressed low levels of GATA3 and higher levels of Tbet.
source: Additionally, we found that these Tr1-like cells also expressed low levels of GATA3 and higher levels of Tbet (Figure 7J, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7J and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Tr1-like cells arise from the allergen-specific memory response in this model.
source: Together, these data indicate that Tr1-like cells arise from the allergen-specific memory response in this model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tetramer staining and memory rechallenge data.

claim: The tetramer-positive cells that produced IL-10 in this model were Tr1-like cells and not Foxp3+ Treg.
source: Further, the tetramer-positive cells that produced IL-10 in this model were Tr1-like cells and not Foxp3+ Treg.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tetramer staining and cytokine production data.

claim: Most CD90.1+ cells exhibited an effector memory phenotype (CD44hi, CD62Llow) upon memory challenge.
source: we observed that most CD90.1+ cells exhibited an effector memory phenotype (CD44hi, CD62Llow) as compared to the CD90.1-Foxp3- cells (Figure 8A).
evidence: This statement is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3- cells had a higher ratio of resident to circulating T cells upon memory challenge.
source: In addition, using intravascular labeling, we found that CD90.1+Foxp3- cells had a higher ratio of resident to circulating T cells (Figure 8B).
evidence: This statement is supported by intravascular labeling data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Disruption of lymphocyte egress did not affect cellular infiltration or eosinophilia in the BAL.
source: We found that disruption of lymphocyte egress did not affect cellular infiltration or eosinophilia in the BAL (Figure 8D,E).
evidence: This statement is supported by FTY720 treatment data shown in Figures 8D and 8E.

claim: The ratio of CD62L+ to CD62L- CD4+ T cells in the lungs was significantly reduced by FTY720 treatment.
source: However, the ratio of CD62L+ to CD62L- CD4+ T cells in the lungs was significantly reduced (Figure 8F).
evidence: This statement is supported by FTY720 treatment data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Lung resident CD62L negative memory cells are sufficient to induce airway inflammation.
source: This is in line with a previous report that lung resident CD62L negative memory cells are sufficient to induce airway inflammation (Hondowicz et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hondowicz et al., 2016.

claim: The frequency of Tr1-like cells within the CD4+T cells in the lungs was unaffected by FTY720 treatment.
source: Notably, the frequency of Tr1-like cells within the CD4+T cells in the lungs was unaffected (Figure 8G).
evidence: This statement is supported by FTY720 treatment data shown in Figure 8G.

claim: Most of the CD90.1+Foxp3- Tr1-like cells were consistently effector memory (CD44hi CD62L low) both with and without FTY270 administration.
source: Unlike CD90.1-Foxp3- T cells, most of the CD90.1+Foxp3- Tr1-like cells were consistently effector memory (CD44hi CD62L low) both with and without FTY270 administration (Figure 8H,I).
evidence: This statement is supported by FTY720 treatment data shown in Figures 8H and 8I.

claim: The majority of CD90.1+Foxp3- CD4+ Tr1-like cells following allergen challenge have a memory phenotype and can arise from lung-resident memory cells.
source: Together, these data indicate that the majority of CD90.1+Foxp3- CD4+ Tr1-like cells following allergen challenge have a memory phenotype and can arise from lung-resident memory cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FTY720 treatment and phenotypic data.

claim: Depletion of CD90.1+ cells during the sensitization phase exacerbated airway inflammation.
source: This exacerbated airway inflammation as measured by total cell and eosinophil infiltration in the BAL (Figure 9C,D) as well as IL-13 production by CD90.1-Foxp3- CD4+T cells (Figure 9E).
evidence: This statement is supported by depletion experiment data shown in Figures 9C, 9D, and 9E.

claim: Depletion of CD90.1+ cells during the memory phase did not impact the inflammatory response.
source: We next depleted the CD90.1+ cell population during the memory phase (Figure 9F,G). This did not impact the inflammatory response (Figure 9H,I), cytokine production by CD90.1-Foxp3- cells (Figure 9J), nor the frequency of tetramer + cells within CD4+T cells in the lungs (Figure 9K).
evidence: This statement is supported by depletion experiment data shown in Figures 9H, 9I, 9J, and 9K.

claim: Transfer of memory Tr1-like cells did not have a beneficial impact on cellular infiltration or eosinophilia in the BAL.
source: Consistent with our observations in the depletion studies, we did not see any beneficial impact of the transfer of memory Tr1-like cells on cellular infiltration or eosinophilia in the BAL (Figure 10A–C).
evidence: This statement is supported by adoptive transfer data shown in Figures 10A-C.

claim: The transferred CD90.1+ T cells were not more likely than transferred CD90.1- T cells to produce IL-10 upon rechallenge with allergen.
source: Moreover, the transferred CD90.1+ T cells were not more likely than transferred CD90.1- T cells to produce IL-10 upon rechallenge with allergen (Figure 10D)
evidence: This statement is supported by adoptive transfer data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: Transferred CD90.1+ T cells did not alter the levels of IL-10 in the lung.
source: and did not alter the levels of IL-10 in the lung (Figure 10E).
evidence: This statement is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 10E.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3- cells could suppress cell infiltration in the BAL when transferred in an acute model.
source: In contrast, CD90.1+Foxp3- cells could suppress cell infiltration in the BAL when transferred in an acute model and were also suppressive in vitro (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by adoptive transfer data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: CD90.1+Foxp3- cells are unable to suppress the allergen specific inflammatory memory responses.
source: This suggests that CD90.1+Foxp3- cells are unable to suppress the allergen specific inflammatory memory responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the adoptive transfer data.

claim: Neither CD90.1+ nor CD90.1 negative cells engraft efficiently in the lungs.
source: An inherent problem of this model is that neither CD90.1+ nor CD90.1 negative cells engraft efficiently in the lungs (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by engraftment data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claim: During primary allergen challenge CD90.1+ cells promote immune tolerance.
source: Together these data indicate that during primary allergen challenge CD90.1+ cells, the majority of which are Tr1-like cells but also include some CD90.1+Foxp3+, promote immune tolerance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the depletion and transfer experiments.

claim: Endogenous Tr1-like cells do not contribute to tolerogenic memory in this model.
source: However, endogenous Tr1-like cells do not contribute to tolerogenic memory in this model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the memory phase depletion and transfer experiments.

claim: Natural Tr1-like cells only transiently express IL-10 after activation.
source: We report that natural Tr1-like cells only transiently express IL-10 after activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic and in vitro culture data.

claim: Cells that actively produce IL-10 are important for immune tolerance to airway allergens.
source: Moreover, while cells that actively produce IL-10 are important for immune tolerance to airway allergens, neither depletion nor transfer of Tr1-like cells altered airway inflammation upon subsequent allergen challenge.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the depletion and transfer experiments.

claim: Naturally-arising Tr1-like cells may promote tolerance but do not contribute to a functionally stable tolerogenic memory population in this model.
source: Together these data suggest that naturally-arising Tr1-like cells may promote tolerance but do not contribute to a functionally stable tolerogenic memory population in this model.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study drawn from all the experimental data.

claim: Persistent antigenic signals were required for maintenance of IL-10 production and expression of Irf1 and Batf.
source: Persistent antigenic signals were required for maintenance of IL-10 production and expression of Irf1 and Batf, transcription factors previously linked to Tr1 status.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vitro culture and transcription factor expression data.

claim: Repeated stimulation may maintain active IL-10 production in airway Tr1-like cells by supporting expression of canonical Tr1 transcription factors.
source: It may be that repeated stimulation, a feature of many immunotherapy regimens, maintains active IL-10 production in airway Tr1-like cells by supporting expression of these canonical Tr1 transcription factors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of immunotherapy.

claim: In the gut, antigen stimulation by commensal bacteria may provide a similar function to maintain IL-10 production.
source: In the gut, a prominent site of IL-10 production, antigen stimulation by commensal bacteria may provide a similar function (Gagliani et al., 2013; Gagliani et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to studies in the gut.

claim: IL-10 production is a temporary phenotype that a fraction of memory T cells adopt upon activation in the setting of certain previously defined differentiation signals.
source: In light of these data, we propose that IL-10 production is a temporary phenotype that a fraction of memory T cells adopt upon activation in the setting of certain previously defined differentiation signals (Wu et al., 2011; Huang et al., 2017; Gregori et al., 2010; Li and Flavell, 2008; Coomes et al., 2017; Brockmann et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a proposed model supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: IL-10 production in response to allergen exposure may be stochastic and not necessarily predicated upon past production of IL-10.
source: Furthermore, IL-10 production in response to allergen exposure may be stochastic and not necessarily predicated upon past production of IL-10.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of IL-10 production.
